gaps.sentence: Who ___ the washing-up in your house?
gaps.explanation: do the washing-up means to wash the dishes; the -s form is needed with 'who'.

gaps.sentence: It's your turn to ___ care of the dog this weekend.
gaps.explanation: take care of somebody/something means to look after them.

gaps.sentence: He was so badly ___ in the fall that he needed an operation.
gaps.explanation: badly hurt is the standard collocation meaning seriously injured.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a fortune by buying his train ticket in advance.
gaps.explanation: save a fortune means to avoid spending a large amount; buying in advance keeps money.

gaps.sentence: He was sent to prison for ___ the law.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'the law' (opposite of obeying it)
gaps.explanation: break the law means to commit a crime; after the preposition 'for' the -ing form is needed.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: Over five hundred athletes will ___ part in the games.
gaps.explanation: take part in something means to participate in it.

gaps.sentence: I only ___ sight of the celebrity for a second before the crowd closed in.
gaps.explanation: catch sight of somebody/something means to notice them briefly.
